## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)). I cannot set labels on this repository; suggested: `orig-external`, `cat-bugfix`, `area:gemm`, `mod-frost`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

`cudnn.triangle_multiplicative_update` serves cc 10.3 with the sm100 body of the LayerNorm-prologue dual GEMM (`ln_prologue.ARCHS_BY_CC[(10, 3)] = "sm100"`). That body pins `frost_compile_options = "--enable-tvm-ffi --gpu-arch sm_100a"`, and an `sm_100a` cubin does not load on cc 10.3. On a B300, every K1 / K3 launch failed with `DSLRuntimeError: ... TVM FFI function is not initialized. Was this function compiled for a different ...`.

Changes:

- `gemm/frost/ln_prologue/__init__.py`:
  - `TARGETS_BY_CC` (`sm_100a` / `sm_103a` / `sm_107a`) and `target_for_cc(cc)`, which gives the same typed decline as `body_arch_for_cc` off a served part.
  - `build_ln_dual_gemm(params, arch, target=None)`: `None` keeps the body's home target (`HOME_TARGETS`) and the loader key every caller has had. Any other target loads its own template module (`load_template(..., extra_key=("gpu_arch", target))`), so the two parts never share a module, its `compile()` cache or a compiled artifact. That module then compiles for the target. A target the body cannot serve raises `ValueError`.
- `triangle_multiplicative_update`: the API passes `target_for_cc(cc)` to `build_trimul_proj` / `build_trimul_tail`, and its per-device plan cache (`_substrate_plan_on`) keys on the target as well.
- Tests:
  - The three suites that build the substrate directly pass the device's target through a `_target()` helper next to `_arch()`.
  - `test_each_served_part_compiles_the_body_for_its_own_target` patches the loader and pins the module key and compile options per target.
  - The SASS probes keep compiling the home body's `sm_100a` text, which is what they inspect.

## Why

The triangle multiplicative update advertises SM103 (`docs/operations/matmul/triangle_multiplicative_update.md`) but could not launch there.

## Related issues

None found.

## API and compatibility impact

None on cc 10.0 or cc 10.7: same target, same module key, same compiled artifacts. On cc 10.3 the API now runs. `build_ln_dual_gemm` / `build_trimul_proj` / `build_trimul_tail` gain an optional trailing `target`.

## Testing

B300 (cc 10.3), develop `64ed3dfe` with its own extension, torch 2.14.1+cu130, cuDNN 9.27.0, CuTe DSL 4.8.1, `CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1`, `python -m pytest -m "L0 or L1" triangle_multiplicative_update/cutedsl` from `test/python`:

| Module | develop | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_trimul_api.py` | 28 passed, 17 failed, 1 skipped | 45 passed, 1 skipped |
| `test_trimul_proj.py` | 36 passed, 22 failed, 36 skipped | 58 passed, 1 failed, 36 skipped |
| `test_trimul_tail.py` | 21 passed, 16 failed | 37 passed |
| `test_trimul_desc_builder.py` | 8 passed | 8 passed |

The failure left on this PR fails on develop as well: `test_the_two_bodies_differ_only_in_the_arch_delta` (`assert (8 > 50)`), a host check of the two body texts that this PR does not touch. Not run on cc 10.0 or cc 10.7, where the target and the module key are unchanged.

Thank you for your contribution! The SM103 target now reaches a separate template module and compiler options. Native SM100 validation passed except for the unchanged body-comparison assertion also reproduced on the baseline. I found one nonblocking device-cache regression when legacy and explicit home-target calls are mixed.

**[P2] Normalize the home target before detecting a device-local compile** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/484ccb4617c641ee6c3d37fead8e4d5e00b85ba1/python/cudnn/triangle_multiplicative_update/api.py#L712))

After build_trimul_proj(params, 'sm100') warms a launch on device 0, an API plan on device 1 now calls the builder with explicit target='sm_100a'. None and 'sm_100a' create different build_ln_dual_gemm cache entries but intentionally share the same template module. The outer cache grows, so built_here is true, even though mod.compile() returned its device-0 launch. This skips the existing device-specific recompile and can return a launch bound to the wrong CUDA context. The analogous home-target alias affects the tail too. Normalize equivalent targets before the cached builder boundary, or determine whether the actual launch was compiled on this device. Add a regression that warms the legacy direct builder before creating an API plan on another device.

Evidence: The real builder, template loader, module compile cache and _substrate_plan_on were exercised with a compiler recorder and modeled device contexts. The explicit-home call added an outer cache entry yet returned the exact launch object recorded on device 0 for a device-1 request. Reusing the same None spelling correctly recompiled for device 1. The baseline's legacy-builder/API sequence also recompiled correctly. A separate SM103 control used a distinct module and recorded sm_103a. No foreign-device binary was launched. Attribution: Introduced by the API's new explicit home-target argument while legacy default-target calls share the module under a distinct outer cache key.

Validation: Exact-head native SM100 triangle-update suite with L0/L1 selected: 163 passed, 22 skipped, 1 failed. The skips were 21 unavailable architecture-disassembly cases and one physical multi-GPU case. Coverage includes API/reference comparisons, projections/tail, graph replay with changed data, bitwise chaining and descriptor checks. The sole failure, test_the_two_bodies_differ_only_in_the_arch_delta, also fails on the baseline with the same assertion. Its test function and both compared kernel bodies are unchanged. The cache probe used real module/cache code with compilation recorded. The SM103 module kept its own target while the home module retained sm_100a. Invalid body/target pairs and target mappings are covered by the new test. Precheck and git diff --check passed. Pipeline 78138481 is running for python/misc; its integration matches all seven changed files. Inspected Style and Security workflows were approved.

Limitations: No independent native SM103 or physical two-GPU execution was available. The author's B300 results are separate evidence. The cache probe establishes incorrect launch reuse; it does not claim a physical cross-device launch reproduction. CI is pending. No GPU performance comparison is claimed; kernel bodies and execute-time arithmetic are unchanged.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

Validation: 46 focused triangle-update API tests passed on native SM100 with L0 and L1 enabled; one physical two-GPU case skipped. This includes the new alias regression, numerical checks, bitwise comparisons, and changed-input CUDA Graph replay. Replayed the independent original cache probe with actual builders, template modules, compile caches, and device-plan caches. A legacy device-0 build followed by the explicit home target on device 1 now recompiles once on device 1; a repeat reuses that plan. The None spelling and distinct SM103 target controls also pass. Only compiler/device contexts were modeled; no foreign-device binary was launched. The warm device-plan cache still returns before the added compile-cache inspection. Kernel arithmetic and the execution path are unchanged by this fix. @@ -55,6 +55,10 @@
 BODIES = {"sm107": "sm107_dual_gemm.py", "sm100": "sm100_dual_gemm.py"}
 ARCHS_BY_CC = {(10, 0): "sm100", (10, 3): "sm100", (10, 7): "sm107"}
 ARCH_GATE_CC = {"sm100": (10, 0), "sm107": (10, 7)}
+#: The arch-specific CuTe target each served part compiles its body for (:func:`target_for_cc`).  A body pins its home part's target
+#: (``HOME_TARGETS``); an ``sm_100a`` cubin does not load on cc 10.3, so that part compiles the sm100 body for ``sm_103a``.
+TARGETS_BY_CC = {(10, 0): "sm_100a", (10, 3): "sm_103a", (10, 7): "sm_107a"}
+HOME_TARGETS = {"sm100": "sm_100a", "sm107": "sm_107a"}
 
 
 def body_arch_for_cc(cc) -> str:
@@ -67,6 +71,12 @@ def body_arch_for_cc(cc) -> str:
     return ARCHS_BY_CC[key]
 
 
+def target_for_cc(cc) -> str:
+    """The CuTe ``--gpu-arch`` target for a device's compute capability (the same typed decline as :func:`body_arch_for_cc` off it)."""
+    body_arch_for_cc(cc)
+    return TARGETS_BY_CC[tuple(int(x) for x in cc)]
+
+
 def ring_stages(arch: str, pairing: str) -> int:
     """The ``arch`` body's operand ring depth for ``pairing`` (:data:`RING_STAGES_BY_ARCH`; a typed decline for an unknown arch or pairing)."""
     if arch not in RING_STAGES_BY_ARCH:
@@ -470,8 +480,9 @@ class LnDualGemmPlan:
 
 
 @lru_cache(maxsize=None)
-def build_ln_dual_gemm(params: LnDualGemmParams, arch: str = "sm107") -> LnDualGemmPlan:
-    """Load the ``arch`` body (:data:`BODIES`; :func:`body_arch_for_cc` names it from the device) specialized for ``params`` and cute-compile it."""
+def build_ln_dual_gemm(params: LnDualGemmParams, arch: str = "sm107", target: Optional[str] = None) -> LnDualGemmPlan:
+    """Load the ``arch`` body (:data:`BODIES`; :func:`body_arch_for_cc` names it from the device) specialized for ``params`` and cute-compile it
+    for ``target`` (:func:`target_for_cc`; None: the body's home target, ``HOME_TARGETS``)."""
     from cudnn.frost.buffers import cutedsl_arch_requirement_error, cutedsl_requirement_error
     from cudnn.frost.template_loader import load_template
 
@@ -485,7 +496,14 @@ def build_ln_dual_gemm(params: LnDualGemmParams, arch: str = "sm107") -> LnDualG
     if msg:
         raise NotImplementedError(msg)
     validate_ln_dual_gemm_params(params, arch)
-    mod = load_template(body_path(arch), params, tag="ln_prologue_dual_gemm")
+    home = HOME_TARGETS[arch]
+    target = home if target is None else target

Thanks. Fixed in c462c3ed (the [P2] home-target cache regression):

- `_substrate_plan_on` no longer infers a fresh compile from the builder cache growing. That cache holds no target, `None` and the home target as separate entries, and all three share one template module and its `compile()`.
- The launch now counts as bound to this device only when the builder cache grew and the module's own `compile()` cache has never hit, that is, when this call compiled it. Any spelling that reaches a module compiled earlier, on any device, gets the per-device recompile.
- `test_a_launch_compiled_on_another_device_is_never_reused_under_another_target_spelling` runs the real builder, template loader and module caches. `torch.cuda.device` only records the device, and `cute.compile` records (device, target) instead of compiling.
  - It warms the proj module through the legacy `build_trimul_proj(params, "sm100")` and the tail module through an explicit `"sm_100a"`, both on cuda:0, then asks for the other spelling on cuda:1. Both compile again for cuda:1, and a repeat reuses that compile.
  - A module first compiled by a plan stays bound to that plan's device, and an `sm_103a` request gets its own module.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `484ccb4617c6` against base `f78022abad7b`.

Thank you for your contribution! The SM103 target now reaches a separate template module and compiler options. Native SM100 validation passed except for the unchanged body-comparison assertion also reproduced on the baseline. I found one nonblocking device-cache regression when legacy and explicit home-target calls are mixed.

**[P2] Normalize the home target before detecting a device-local compile** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/484ccb4617c641ee6c3d37fead8e4d5e00b85ba1/python/cudnn/triangle_multiplicative_update/api.py#L712))

After build_trimul_proj(params, 'sm100') warms a launch on device 0, an API plan on device 1 now calls the builder with explicit target='sm_100a'. None and 'sm_100a' create different build_ln_dual_gemm cache entries but intentionally share the same template module. The outer cache grows, so built_here is true, even though mod.compile() returned its device-0 launch. This skips the existing device-specific recompile and can return a launch bound to the wrong CUDA context. The analogous home-target alias affects the tail too. Normalize equivalent targets before the cached builder boundary, or determine whether the actual launch was compiled on this device. Add a regression that warms the legacy direct builder before creating an API plan on another device.

Evidence: The real builder, template loader, module compile cache and _substrate_plan_on were exercised with a compiler recorder and modeled device contexts. The explicit-home call added an outer cache entry yet returned the exact launch object recorded on device 0 for a device-1 request. Reusing the same None spelling correctly recompiled for device 1. The baseline's legacy-builder/API sequence also recompiled correctly. A separate SM103 control used a distinct module and recorded sm_103a. No foreign-device binary was launched. Attribution: Introduced by the API's new explicit home-target argument while legacy default-target calls share the module under a distinct outer cache key.

Validation: Exact-head native SM100 triangle-update suite with L0/L1 selected: 163 passed, 22 skipped, 1 failed. The skips were 21 unavailable architecture-disassembly cases and one physical multi-GPU case. Coverage includes API/reference comparisons, projections/tail, graph replay with changed data, bitwise chaining and descriptor checks. The sole failure, test_the_two_bodies_differ_only_in_the_arch_delta, also fails on the baseline with the same assertion. Its test function and both compared kernel bodies are unchanged. The cache probe used real module/cache code with compilation recorded. The SM103 module kept its own target while the home module retained sm_100a. Invalid body/target pairs and target mappings are covered by the new test. Precheck and git diff --check passed. Pipeline 78138481 is running for python/misc; its integration matches all seven changed files. Inspected Style and Security workflows were approved.

Limitations: No independent native SM103 or physical two-GPU execution was available. The author's B300 results are separate evidence. The cache probe establishes incorrect launch reuse; it does not claim a physical cross-device launch reproduction. CI is pending. No GPU performance comparison is claimed; kernel bodies and execute-time arithmetic are unchanged.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
